- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias in the first few days, then plateau or slightly decline — true prices rise sharply and sustain higher levels.
- After a spike in true prices (e.g., 95+), model forecasts often overshoot initially but then fail to sustain the peak, underestimating the continuation of high prices.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — it tends to forecast downward trends even when true prices are trending upward.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements, particularly in the 10–15 day window — model is slow to react to new information.
- Model overfits to recent low prices, failing to recognize that recent lows are often followed by strong rebounds.
- In cases of sustained high prices, model fails to capture the full magnitude of the trend — underestimates peak values and duration.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — true prices show sharp spikes and drops, but model flattens them out, leading to underestimation of risk and upside potential.
